high.title: Six Major Life Insurers Record Over 584 Billion NT in New Contract Premiums in February
high.summary: Continuing strong sales momentum from January's record performance, Taiwan's six major life insurance companies achieved combined new contract premiums exceeding 584 billion NT in February, representing a 41% year-over-year increase. The growth was primarily driven by investment-linked policies and participating policies. For the first two months of 2026, combined new contract premiums reached over 1.704 trillion NT, up 70.8% year-over-year. Industry analysts note this reflects strong investor confidence amid Taiwan's robust stock market performance. However, February volumes declined from January's record 1.11 trillion NT due to fewer working days from Lunar New Year and holidays. Key performers included Cathay Life (209.5 billion NT, +32.5% YoY), Fubon Life (114.4 billion NT, +6% YoY), and Taiwan Life (76 billion NT, +98% YoY). The strong performance indicates healthy appetite for insurance products despite geopolitical uncertainties, with investment-linked and USD-denominated policies particularly popular among consumers seeking portfolio diversification.

high.title: US-Iran War Triggers Historic Foreign Investment Outflow of 120.8 Billion NT from Taiwan Stocks
high.summary: Foreign investors executed a record-breaking single-day sell-off of 120.8 billion NT from Taiwan stocks on March 9, marking the largest daily outflow in market history as Middle East tensions escalated. The massive liquidation saw foreign investors dump major holdings including 37,837 shares of TSMC (67.8 billion NT), 63.5 billion NT of Hon Hai, and 37.09 billion NT of MediaTek. Most significantly, foreign investors aggressively sold Taiwan 50 ETF (0050) with 200,178 thousand shares disposed, continuing a pattern of using index products for rapid exits. The sell-off reflects global risk-off sentiment as Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz pushed oil prices toward $120/barrel. Interestingly, foreign capital showed a "large-to-small" rotation strategy, buying into mid-cap stocks like ADATA (3.86 billion NT), Phison (2.21 billion NT), and Winbond Electronics (2.16 billion NT) while dumping mega-cap stocks. This historic outflow underscores the vulnerability of Taiwan's market to geopolitical shocks and highlights the critical role of domestic institutional investors in market stability.

high.title: Taiwan's Central Bank Faces Monetary Policy Dilemma Amid Oil Price Surge
high.summary: Cathay Securities Investment Trust CEO Chang Yung-chuan warned that the Central Bank of Taiwan faces a complex monetary policy challenge as oil price surges to $90+ per barrel threaten to reignite inflation concerns while maintaining economic growth momentum. Chang emphasized that unlike the 1970s oil crises, today's energy price impact on consumer prices is significantly reduced due to structural economic changes. He maintains optimism that the Fed still has room for 50 basis points of rate cuts in the second half of 2026, particularly after new Fed Chairman Warsh takes office, providing clearer monetary policy direction. Chang noted that while the Middle East conflict may delay Fed rate cuts, the underlying trend of declining core inflation remains intact. For Taiwan's monetary policy, this creates a delicate balancing act between supporting domestic growth and managing imported inflation pressures. The CBC will likely maintain its cautious approach, closely monitoring both global oil price developments and domestic inflation dynamics. Market participants should expect continued volatility in Taiwan's interest rate outlook as geopolitical tensions persist.

medium.title: National Development Fund and Public Banks Execute Record 77.4 Billion NT Stock Purchases
medium.summary: Taiwan's "national team" of eight major state-owned banks mounted an unprecedented rescue operation, purchasing a record 77.4 billion NT worth of stocks last week as foreign investors dumped 317 billion NT. The intervention demonstrates strong government commitment to market stability during the US-Iran conflict crisis.

medium.title: Taiwan Stock Exchange Emphasizes Fundamentals Remain Strong Despite 9.33% Decline
medium.summary: Taiwan Stock Exchange issued a statement emphasizing that despite the 9.33% decline since the US-Iran war began, Taiwan's market has shown relative resilience compared to regional peers. The exchange noted that 558 listed companies reported February revenues totaling 2.31 trillion NT, up 19.75% year-over-year, demonstrating strong underlying fundamentals.

medium.title: TSMC February Revenue Falls Below 400 Billion NT But Analysts Remain Optimistic on Q1 Guidance
medium.summary: TSMC reported February consolidated revenue of 317.66 billion NT, down 20.8% month-over-month but still the strongest February on record. Cumulative first two months revenue reached 718.91 billion NT, up 29.9% year-over-year. Analysts believe TSMC remains on track to exceed Q1 guidance despite the February decline.

medium.title: Taiwan Life Insurance Industry February New Contract Premiums Show Resilience
medium.summary: Despite Middle East geopolitical tensions, Taiwan's life insurance industry maintained strong momentum in February with over 584 billion NT in new contract premiums. Investment-linked and participating policies led growth, with the industry showing remarkable resilience to market volatility. Analysts expect continued strength if equity markets stabilize.
